questions.q: What does PowerShell DSC (Desired State Configuration) actually do?
options: Lets you declare the state a system should be in, then has an engine repeatedly reconcile the system to that state
Runs a one-time script and exits, with no concept of ongoing state
Only manages Windows Registry keys, not applications like SQL Server
Replaces PowerShell entirely with a new scripting language
questions.explain: DSC's defining feature is continuous reconciliation toward a declared desired state, not a one-shot script run.

options: DSC resources for common SQL Server-specific configuration settings, such as max degree of parallelism
A GUI replacement for SQL Server Management Studio
A backup and restore engine unrelated to configuration
A licensing management tool for SQL Server editions
questions.explain: SqlServerDsc is the open-source DSC resource module that exposes SQL Server settings as declarative resources.

questions.q: What is the key practical difference between a declarative DSC resource and an imperative script that runs `sp_configure` once?
options: The declarative resource can be safely re-applied on a schedule and is a no-op if the setting already matches; the imperative script has no idea whether it already matches
There is no real difference — both behave identically
The imperative script is always faster to write and maintain
DSC resources cannot set any value that sp_configure can set
questions.explain: Idempotent re-application without unintended side effects is the core value of the declarative approach.

questions.q: What real-world problem does re-applying a declarative configuration resource on a recurring schedule catch?
options: Configuration drift — someone manually changing a setting after it was first set correctly
Disk space running low on the server
Network latency between the DBA's workstation and the server
SQL Server license expiration
questions.explain: Scheduled reconciliation catches manual changes that would otherwise silently drift a server away from its intended configuration.

questions.q: How does the lesson describe Ansible-style configuration management relative to PowerShell DSC?
options: A comparable category following the same declarative-state idea, using YAML playbooks instead of DSC resources, without claiming specific product syntax details
A Microsoft product that directly replaces DSC in all environments
A tool that only works with MySQL, never SQL Server
An exact syntactic clone of PowerShell DSC
questions.explain: The lesson names the category honestly as an alternative following the same principle, without overclaiming exact feature parity or syntax.
